chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Khattab al-Awr, from Abu Hamza, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Connecting with the relatives purifies the deeds, increases the wealth, repels the afflictions, eases the Reckoning, and delays the death.'

key_terms.تُيَسِّرُ الْحِسَابَ: Eases the Reckoning (accounting on Judgment Day)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and worldly benefits of maintaining good relations with relatives in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) outlines the spiritual and worldly benefits of maintaining kinship ties (silat al-arham), noting that it purifies deeds, increases wealth, wards off calamities, facilitates the Day of Judgment accounting, and prolongs lifespan. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for understanding 'silat al-arham' not merely as social courtesy but as a mechanism for divine mercy and material barakah. The emphasis on 'facilitating the accounting' (tuyassiru al-hisab) highlights the direct link between social ethics and eschatological ease.
